brief: ZeroHedge summarizes Goldman Sachs strategist Louis Miller's Global Reflections note. Goldman expects a 25bp September hike but argues the cycle ends early because inflation is supposed to roll over, leaving term premium, driven by the war, hyperscaler issuance, repatriation and a new Fed chair, as the rates risk. Oil is near $105 and the 10-year near 5%. Miller says positioning and risk appetite are objectively neutral, so there is fuel for more risk-taking, and profitability ex rates might argue for 20x multiples. The trade is long the AI complex hedged with the ex-AI book: AI valuations de-rated 30-40%, the AI vs AI at Risk pair is up 14% month to date but 38% off highs, and Miller is most convicted the long leg rallies on earnings momentum. Power is the cleanest expression, its long/short ratio in the 4th percentile, and renewables weakness is overdone. Consumer stays pressured by rates, oil and agentic AI eroding switching costs. Housing call spreads, Japan and Greek banks and Brazil baskets are the other expressions. The article's own bear case is that single 25bp hikes are rare and that $105 oil with a 5% 10-year compresses margins.
